source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Carrying fairly little established role in the overall evaluation of a client with suspected pulmonary embolism in most clinical settings","B":"Has strong negative predictive value in appropriately selected clients, helping rule out pulmonary embolism in lower-risk clients, though it is nonspecific if positive","C":"Definitively confirming the presence of a pulmonary embolism fully on its own, without needing any further confirmatory imaging","D":"Needing to be followed by further imaging studies in nearly every single case, without much regard for the result or clinical probability score"}}
source_row.rationale: A negative D-dimer result has strong negative predictive value in appropriately selected (lower clinical probability) clients, helping rule out pulmonary embolism without further imaging, though this test is nonspecific if positive (many conditions can elevate D-dimer), requiring further imaging in that circumstance.
